#!/usr/sbin/nft -f
# ovid-sandbox egress filter — generated by render-nft; do not hand-edit.
# Reload-safe: the declare-then-delete guard below removes any previous
# version of the table, so every load starts from a clean state.
table inet ovid_sandbox
delete table inet ovid_sandbox

table inet ovid_sandbox {
	set blocked_v4 {
		type ipv4_addr
		flags interval
		elements = { 0.0.0.0/8, 10.0.0.0/8, 100.64.0.0/10, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.0.0/16, 172.16.0.0/12, 192.0.0.0/24, 192.168.0.0/16, 198.18.0.0/15, 224.0.0.0/4, 240.0.0.0/4 }
	}

	set blocked_v6 {
		type ipv6_addr
		flags interval
		auto-merge
		elements = { ::/128, ::1/128, ::/104, ::a00:0/104, ::6440:0/106, ::7f00:0/104, ::a9fe:0/112, ::ac10:0/108, ::c000:0/120, ::c0a8:0/112, ::c612:0/111, ::e000:0/100, ::f000:0/100, ::ffff:0:0/96, fe80::/10, fc00::/7, fec0::/10, ff00::/8, 2002::/16, 64:ff9b::/96 }
	}

	chain output {
		type filter hook output priority 0; policy accept;

		# sandbox uids 200000-209999 — internal nets and this host's public IP are blocked
		meta skuid 200000-209999 ip daddr @blocked_v4 counter drop
		meta skuid 200000-209999 ip6 daddr @blocked_v6 counter drop
		meta skuid 200000-209999 ip daddr 203.0.113.7 counter drop

		# sandbox uids 200000-209999 — outbound allow-list, then deny the remainder
		meta skuid 200000-209999 tcp dport { 53, 80, 443 } counter accept
		meta skuid 200000-209999 udp dport { 53 } counter accept
		meta skuid 200000-209999 counter drop
	}
}
